body:
For an ideal gas at fixed volume, doubling absolute temperature makes pressure

A. half
B. unchanged
C. double
D. four times

Choices:
A. half
B. unchanged
C. double
D. four times

During an isothermal expansion of an ideal gas, its internal-energy change is

A. positive
B. negative
C. zero
D. equal to pressure

Choices:
A. positive
B. negative
C. zero
D. equal to pressure

Which of the following best explains why energy is spontaneously transferred from a hot object to a cold object?

A. decreases total entropy
B. increases total entropy
C. violates energy conservation
D. decreases the entropy of the cold object

Choices:
A. decreases total entropy
B. increases total entropy
C. violates energy conservation
D. decreases the entropy of the cold object

The electric field direction at a point is the direction of force on

A. a positive test charge
B. a negative test charge
C. any neutral object
D. an electron only

Choices:
A. a positive test charge
B. a negative test charge
C. any neutral object
D. an electron only

Moving a positive charge opposite a uniform electric field causes electric potential energy to

A. decrease
B. increase
C. remain zero
D. become mass

Choices:
A. decrease
B. increase
C. remain zero
D. become mass

Two identical positive point charges are separated. At their midpoint the electric field is

A. zero
B. toward the left charge
C. toward the right charge
D. infinite

Choices:
A. zero
B. toward the left charge
C. toward the right charge
D. infinite

Two resistors 3 Ω and 6 Ω in parallel have equivalent resistance

A. 2 Ω
B. 3 Ω
C. 9 Ω
D. 18 Ω

Choices:
A. 2 Ω
B. 3 Ω
C. 9 Ω
D. 18 Ω

A 12 V battery drives 3 A through a resistor. Its resistance is

A. 0.25 Ω
B. 4 Ω
C. 9 Ω
D. 36 Ω

Choices:
A. 0.25 Ω
B. 4 Ω
C. 9 Ω
D. 36 Ω

Immediately after an uncharged capacitor is connected through a resistor to a battery, the capacitor behaves approximately like

A. an open circuit
B. a wire
C. a charged battery
D. an inductor

Choices:
A. an open circuit
B. a wire
C. a charged battery
D. an inductor

A photon has energy

A. rest energy m0c²
B. hf
C. qV always
D. p²/2m

Choices:
A. rest energy m0c²
B. hf
C. qV always
D. p²/2m

At fixed temperature and volume, doubling the number of ideal-gas molecules makes pressure

A. half as large
B. unchanged
C. twice as large
D. four times as large

Choices:
A. half as large
B. unchanged
C. twice as large
D. four times as large

Two rods have equal dimensions and temperature difference. Rod A has twice Rod B's thermal conductivity. The steady conduction rate through A is

A. half as large
B. the same
C. twice as large
D. four times as large

Choices:
A. half as large
B. the same
C. twice as large
D. four times as large

Two different ideal gases initially separated at the same temperature mix in an insulated container. The total entropy

A. decreases
B. stays constant
C. increases
D. becomes zero

Choices:
A. decreases
B. stays constant
C. increases
D. becomes zero

Identical isolated conducting spheres carry charges +6Q and 0. They touch and separate. After separating, the two spheres' charges are

A. +6Q and 0
B. +3Q and +3Q
C. +6Q and +6Q
D. 0 and 0

Choices:
A. +6Q and 0
B. +3Q and +3Q
C. +6Q and +6Q
D. 0 and 0

At a point where electric potential is zero, the electric field

A. must be zero
B. must be constant nearby
C. may be nonzero
D. must point toward that point

Choices:
A. must be zero
B. must be constant nearby
C. may be nonzero
D. must point toward that point

An electron accelerated from rest through a potential difference magnitude ΔV gains kinetic energy equal to:

Choices:
A. eΔV
B. (1/2)eΔV
C. 2eΔV
D. -eΔV

The voltage across a fixed resistor is doubled. Its power dissipation becomes

A. half
B. twice
C. four times
D. unchanged

Choices:
A. half
B. twice
C. four times
D. unchanged

Traversing an ideal battery from its negative terminal to its positive terminal in a loop equation contributes

A. +emf
B. -emf
C. zero
D. depends on the current direction

Choices:
A. +emf
B. -emf
C. zero
D. depends on the current direction

Currents 2.0 A and 3.5 A enter a junction. If one current leaves, its magnitude is

A. 1.5 A
B. 2.75 A
C. 5.5 A
D. 3.5 A

Choices:
A. 1.5 A
B. 2.75 A
C. 5.5 A
D. 3.5 A

A capacitor in series with a resistor has been connected to a DC battery for a very long time. The circuit current is

A. battery voltage divided by R
B. zero
C. infinite
D. set only by C

Choices:
A. battery voltage divided by R
B. zero
C. infinite
D. set only by C
